   59\t    return Pdf(sanitize_filename(stem), data)\n=== app/rendering.py\n     1\t\"\"\"Markdown to safe HTML: the one pipeline every rendering of user-written\n     2\tMarkdown goes through, the admin preview now and the public export later.\n     3\t\n     4\tmarkdown-it-py renders (raw HTML in the Markdown is let through to it), then\n     5\tnh3 sanitizes, dropping <script>, event-handler attributes, javascript: URLs,\n     6\tand anything else not on its allowlist. The stored body stays raw; only this\n     7\tfunction's output is ever marked safe.\n     8\t\n     9\tTwo additions to nh3's allowlist, both for Markdown tables:\n    10\t  - `style` on a table cell, but only as exactly `text-align:left|right|center`,\n    11\t    so a column's alignment (`|---:|`) survives and nothing else does.\n    12\t  - the class TABLE_SCROLL on a <div>: each Markdown table is wrapped in one, so\n    13\t    a wide table can scroll sideways without restyling the <table> itself.\n    14\t\"\"\"\n    15\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n    16\t\n    17\timport re\n    18\t\n    19\timport nh3\n    20\tfrom markdown_it import MarkdownIt\n    21\tfrom markupsafe import Markup\n    22\t\n    23\tTABLE_SCROLL = \"content-table-scroll\"\n    24\t\n    25\t_MARKDOWN = MarkdownIt(\"commonmark\").enable(\"table\")\n    26\t_MARKDOWN.add_render_rule(\"table_open\", lambda self, tokens, idx, options, env: (\n    27\t    f'<div class=\"{TABLE_SCROLL}\">\\n' + self.renderToken(tokens, idx, options, env)))\n    28\t_MARKDOWN.add_render_rule(\"table_close\", lambda self, tokens, idx, options, env: (\n    29\t    self.renderToken(tokens, idx, options, env) + \"</div>\\n\"))\n    30\t\n    31\t_TABLE_CELLS = (\"th\", \"td\")\n    32\t_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES = {**nh3.ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES,\n    33\t                       **{cell: nh3.ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES.get(cell, set()) | {\"style\"}\n    34\t                          for cell in _TABLE_CELLS}}\n    35\t_TEXT_ALIGN = re.compile(r\"\\s*text-align\\s*:\\s*(left|right|center)\\s*\", re.I)\n    36\t\n    37\t\n    38\tdef _cell_alignment(tag: str, attribute: str, value: str) -> str | None:\n    39\t    \"\"\"Keep a table cell's `style` only as its text-align, and only if that is\n    40\t    one of the three a Markdown table writes; drop every other declaration.\"\"\"\n    41\t    if attribute != \"style\":\n    42\t        return value\n    43\t    if tag not in _TABLE_CELLS:\n    44\t        return None\n    45\t    for declaration in value.split(\";\"):\n    46\t        if match := _TEXT_ALIGN.fullmatch(declaration):\n    47\t            return f\"text-align:{match.group(1).lower()}\"\n    48\t    return None\n    49\t\n    50\t\n    51\tdef render_markdown(text: str) -> Markup:\n    52\t    return Markup(nh3.clean(_MARKDOWN.render(text or \"\"),\n    53\t                            attributes=_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES,\n    54\t                            attribute_filter=_cell_alignment,\n    55\t                            allowed_classes={\"div\": {TABLE_SCROLL}}))\n=== app/public_site.py\n     1\t\"\"\"The public site: every page a visitor can see, each described by the path\n     2\tit has in the exported site (e.g. \"data-bites/fall-enrollment.html\").\n     3\t\n     4\tThe app serves these pages at those same paths (app.routes.public), and\n     5\t`cms publish` writes them there (app.publish), so the two render one set of pages\n     6\trather than two. Pages link to each other relatively, through `root` (\"\" at\n     7\tthe top of the site, \"../\" one folder down), so the same HTML works served\n     8\tfrom / and exported to a GitHub Pages subfolder. Where each kind of page or\n     9\tfile sits is decided here, by the *_path functions, and nowhere else.\n    10\t\n    11\tContent is read only through the published-only queries (`list_published`,\n    12\t`get_published`), so a draft cannot reach a page, a link, or the navigation.\n    13\t\"\"\"\n    14\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n    15\t\n    16\timport sqlite3\n    17\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n    18\tfrom pathlib import Path\n    19\t\n    20\tfrom app import data_bites, reports, settings\n    21\tfrom app.templating import templates\n    22\t\n    23\tCSS = \"\"\"/* The public site's one stylesheet, at style.css in the site's root. */\n    24\t:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\n    25\tbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\n    26\t.header-home { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\n    27\t.nav-site ul { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.25rem 1rem; list-style: none; margin: 0.5rem 0 0; padding: 0; }\n    28\tmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n    29\t/* Markdown tables, in a Data Bite's or Report's body. A wide one scrolls\n    30\t   sideways in its wrapper (app.rendering.TABLE_SCROLL) rather than widening\n    31\t   the page; on a phone, rather than squeezing its text to a word a line. */\n    32\t.content-body .content-table-scroll { margin-block: 1rem; overflow-x: auto; }\n    33\t.content-body table { border-collapse: collapse; }\n    34\t.content-body th, .content-body td { border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 30%, transparent); padding: 0.35rem 0.7rem; }\n    35\t.content-body th { background: color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 8%, transparent); font-weight: 600; }\n    36\t@media (max-width: 40rem) { .content-body th, .content-body td { min-width: 10ch; } }\n    37\t\"\"\"\n    38\tRECENT_DATA_BITES = 5  # on the home page; the rest are on the Data Bites list\n    39\t\n    40\t\n    41\tdef data_bite_path(slug: str) -> str:\n    42\t    return f\"data-bites/{slug}.html\"\n    43\t\n    44\t\n    45\tdef report_path(slug: str) -> str:\n    46\t    return f\"reports/{slug}.html\"\n    47\t\n    48\t\n    49\tdef report_file_path(slug: str) -> str:\n    50\t    # .pdf, not the upload's own extension: a Report's file is always a PDF (T05).\n    51\t    return f\"reports/files/{slug}.pdf\"\n    52\t\n    53\t\n    54\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n    55\tclass Page:\n    56\t    path: str      # where the page sits in the site, relative to its root\n    57\t    template: str\n    58\t    context: dict = field(default_factory=dict)\n    59\t\n    60\t    def render(self) -> str:\n    61\t        root = \"../\" * self.path.count(\"/\")\n    62\t        return templates.env.get_template(self.template).render(\n    63\t            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, root=root, css_path=f\"{root}style.css\",\n    64\t            home_path=f\"{root}index.html\", nav_reports=reports.list_published(),\n    65\t            data_bite_path=data_bite_path, report_path=report_path,\n    66\t            report_file_path=report_file_path, **self.context)\n    67\t\n    68\t\n    69\tdef home() -> Page:\n    70\t    return Page(\"index.html\", \"public/home.html\",\n    71\t                {\"data_bites\": data_bites.list_published()[:RECENT_DATA_BITES]})\n    72\t\n    73\t\n    74\tdef data_bite_list() -> Page:\n    75\t    return Page(\"data-bites/index.html\", \"public/data_bites.html\",\n    76\t                {\"page_title\": \"Data Bites\", \"data_bites\": data_bites.list_published()})\n    77\t\n    78\t\n    79\tdef data_bite(slug: str) -> Page | None:\n    80\t    \"\"\"A published Data Bite's page; None for a draft or no such Data Bite.\"\"\"\n    81\t    bite = data_bites.get_published(slug)\n    82\t    return None if bite is None else _data_bite_page(bite)\n    83\t\n    84\t\n    85\tdef _data_bite_page(bite: sqlite3.Row) -> Page:\n    86\t    return Page(data_bite_path(bite[\"slug\"]), \"public/data_bite.html\",\n    87\t                {\"page_title\": bite[\"title\"], \"bite\": bite})\n    88\t\n    89\t\n    90\tdef report_list() -> Page:\n    91\t    return Page(\"reports/index.html\", \"public/reports.html\",\n    92\t                {\"page_title\": \"Reports\", \"reports\": reports.list_published()})\n    93\t\n    94\t\n    95\tdef _stored_file(report: sqlite3.Row) -> Path | None:\n    96\t    \"\"\"Where the Report's file is stored, if it has one and it is there.\"\"\"\n    97\t    if report[\"file_name\"] is None:\n    98\t        return None\n    99\t    stored = reports.file_path(report[\"id\"])\n   100\t    return stored if stored.is_file() else None\n   101\t\n   102\t\n   103\tdef report(slug: str) -> Page | None:\n   104\t    \"\"\"A published Report's page, linking its file only if that can be\n   105\t    downloaded; None for a draft or no such Report.\"\"\"\n   106\t    found = reports.get_published(slug)\n   107\t    return None if found is None else _report_page(found)\n   108\t\n   109\t\n   110\tdef _report_page(found: sqlite3.Row) -> Page:\n   111\t    return Page(report_path(found[\"slug\"]), \"public/report.html\",\n   112\t                {\"page_title\": found[\"title\"], \"report\": found,\n   113\t                 \"has_file\": _stored_file(found) is not None})\n   114\t\n   115\t\n   116\tdef report_file(slug: str) -> tuple[Path, str] | None:\n   117\t    \"\"\"A published Report's attached file, at report_file_path(slug) in the\n   118\t    site, as (where it is stored, its display name). None for a draft, a\n   119\t    Report with no file, or no such Report.\"\"\"\n   120\t    found = reports.get_published(slug)\n   121\t    stored = found and _stored_file(found)\n   122\t    return (stored, found[\"file_name\"]) if stored else None\n   123\t\n   124\t\n   125\tdef pages() -> list[Page]:\n   126\t    \"\"\"Every page of the site: what `cms publish` writes.\"\"\"\n   127\t    return [home(), data_bite_list(), report_list(),\n   128\t            *map(_data_bite_page, data_bites.list_published()),\n   129\t            *map(_report_page, reports.list_published())]\n   130\t\n   131\t\n   132\tdef files() -> dict[str, Path]:\n   133\t    \"\"\"Every file the site's pages link to besides the stylesheet, as\n   134\t    {path in the site: where it is stored}: the published Reports' files.\"\"\"\n   135\t    stored = {found[\"slug\"]: _stored_file(found) for found in reports.list_published()}\n   136\t    return {report_file_path(slug): path for slug, path in stored.items() if path}\n=== app/publish.py\n     1\t\"\"\"`cms publish`: write the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n     2\t\n     3\tThe pages and files come from app.public_site, the same ones the app serves,\n     4\tat the same paths, so the export is the live public site rather than a second\n     5\trendering of it. That module reads only published content and links only\n     6\trelatively, which gives the two rules the rubric checks here:\n     7\t\n     8\t  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n     9\t  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"reports/x.html\"), never\n    10\t     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n    11\t\"\"\"\n    12\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n    13\t\n    14\timport shutil\n    15\tfrom pathlib import Path\n    16\t\n    17\tfrom app import public_site, settings\n    18\t\n    19\t\n    20\tdef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    21\t    \"\"\"Regenerate `out` (site/ by default) from scratch, so a page taken down\n    22\t    since the last publish is gone from it too.\"\"\"\n    23\t    out = out or settings.SITE\n    24\t    if out.exists():\n    25\t        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    26\t    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    27\t    # UTF-8, as the app serves them, whatever this machine's locale.\n    28\t    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(public_site.CSS, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    29\t    for page in public_site.pages():\n    30\t        _target(out, page.path).write_text(page.render(), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    31\t    for path, stored in public_site.files().items():\n    32\t        shutil.copyfile(stored, _target(out, path))\n    33\t    return out\n    34\t\n    35\t\n    36\tdef _target(out: Path, path: str) -> Path:\n    37\t    \"\"\"Where `path` in the site goes under `out`, its folder made.\"\"\"\n    38\t    target = out / path\n    39\t    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    40\t    return target\n=== app/db.py\n     1\t\"\"\"SQLite access. Every table's schema lives here, so init_db() builds them all.\"\"\"\n     2\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n     3\t\n     4\timport sqlite3\n     5\tfrom collections.abc import Iterator\n     6\tfrom contextlib import contextmanager\n     7\t\n     8\tfrom app import settings\n     9\t\n    10\tSCHEMA = \"\"\"\n    11\tCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (\n    12\t    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    13\t    email         TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,\n    14\t    name          TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    15\t    role          TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    16\t    password_hash TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    17\t    is_active     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n    18\t    created_at    TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n    19\t);\n    20\t\n    21\tCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS data_bites (\n    22\t    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    23\t    title      TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    24\t    slug       TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    25\t    body       TEXT    NOT NULL,  -- raw Markdown; sanitized only when rendered\n    26\t    status     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')),\n    27\t    author_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id),\n    28\t    created_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    29\t    updated_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n    30\t);\n    31\t\n    32\tCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reports (\n    33\t    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    34\t    title      TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    35\t    slug       TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- unique among Reports only; a Data Bite may share it\n    36\t    body       TEXT    NOT NULL,  -- raw Markdown; sanitized only when rendered\n    37\t    status     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')),\n    38\t    author_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id),\n    39\t    created_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    40\t    updated_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    41\t    file_name  TEXT    -- the attached PDF's sanitized name for display; NULL if none\n    42\t);\n    43\t\"\"\"\n    44\t\n    45\t# Columns added after a table was first created: (table, column, definition).\n    46\t# CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS leaves an existing table alone, so init_db adds\n    47\t# any of these an older database is missing.\n    48\tADDED_COLUMNS = [\n    49\t    (\"reports\", \"file_name\", \"TEXT\"),\n    50\t]\n    51\t\n    52\t\n    53\t@contextmanager\n    54\tdef connect() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n    55\t    \"\"\"Open the database named by settings (read at call time, so tests can swap\n    56\t    it). Commits on success, rolls back on error, always closes.\"\"\"\n    57\t    conn = sqlite3.connect(settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    58\t    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    59\t    conn.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON\")\n    60\t    try:\n    61\t        with conn:\n    62\t            yield conn\n    63\t    finally:\n    64\t        conn.close()\n    65\t\n    66\t\n    67\tdef init_db() -> None:\n    68\t    with connect() as conn:\n    69\t        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n    70\t        for table, column, definition in ADDED_COLUMNS:\n    71\t            existing = {row[\"name\"] for row in conn.execute(f\"PRAGMA table_info({table})\")}\n    72\t            if column not in existing:\n    73\t                conn.execute(f\"ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {column} {definition}\")\n=== app/content.py\n     1\t\"\"\"What Data Bites and Reports share: the title/slug/Markdown-body fields, their\n     2\tvalidation, the draft/published status, and the table-level reads and writes.\n     3\t\n     4\tEach content type keeps its own table, so a slug is unique within a type but a\n     5\tData Bite and a Report may share one (spec #1, \"Publish gate & export paths\":\n     6\texports are namespaced by type). Who may do what is decided by each type's own\n     7\tmodule and routes, not here.\n     8\t\"\"\"\n     9\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n    10\t\n    11\timport re\n    12\timport sqlite3\n    13\tfrom collections.abc import Callable\n    14\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n    15\t\n    16\tfrom app import db\n    17\t\n    18\tSTATUS_LABELS = {\"draft\": \"Draft\", \"published\": \"Published\"}\n    19\t# Runs inside the transaction that wrote an item's row, given the connection and\n    20\t# the item's id; if it raises, the row's change is rolled back with it.\n    21\tAlsoWrite = Callable[[sqlite3.Connection, int], None]\n    22\t_SLUG_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*\")\n    23\t# A slug names its item's page, <type folder>/<slug>.html, on the public site;\n    24\t# <type folder>/index.html is taken by the type's list page.\n    25\t_RESERVED_SLUGS = {\"index\"}\n    26\t\n    27\t\n    28\tclass ContentError(ValueError):\n    29\t    \"\"\"Content broke a rule; the message is safe to show.\"\"\"\n    30\t\n    31\t\n    32\tclass DuplicateSlug(ContentError):\n    33\t    pass\n    34\t\n    35\t\n    36\tdef validate(title: str, slug: str, body: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]:\n    37\t    title, slug = title.strip(), slug.strip()\n    38\t    if not title:\n    39\t        raise ContentError(\"Enter a title.\")\n    40\t    if not _SLUG_PATTERN.fullmatch(slug):\n    41\t        raise ContentError(\"Slugs use lowercase letters, digits, and single \"\n    42\t                           \"hyphens, e.g. fall-enrollment.\")\n    43\t    if slug in _RESERVED_SLUGS:\n    44\t        raise ContentError(f\"The slug {slug} is reserved for the list page; \"\n    45\t                           \"choose another.\")\n    46\t    if not body.strip():\n    47\t        raise ContentError(\"Enter a body.\")\n    48\t    return title, slug, body\n    49\t\n    50\t\n    51\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n    52\tclass ContentTable:\n    53\t    \"\"\"One content type's table. `table` is a fixed identifier from this\n    54\t    codebase, never user input.\"\"\"\n    55\t    table: str  # e.g. \"reports\"\n    56\t    noun: str   # e.g. \"Report\", for messages\n    57\t\n    58\t    def _select(self, where: str, order: str, params: tuple = ()) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    59\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n    60\t            return conn.execute(\n    61\t                f\"SELECT c.*, u.name AS author_name FROM {self.table} c\"\n    62\t                f\" JOIN users u ON u.id = c.author_id WHERE {where} ORDER BY {order}\",\n    63\t                params,\n    64\t            ).fetchall()\n    65\t\n    66\t    def _duplicate_slug_error(self, exc: sqlite3.IntegrityError, slug: str) -> DuplicateSlug:\n    67\t        \"\"\"Translate the slug's UNIQUE violation; re-raise any other constraint.\"\"\"\n    68\t        if f\"{self.table}.slug\" not in str(exc):\n    69\t            raise exc\n    70\t        return DuplicateSlug(f\"Another {self.noun} already uses the slug {slug}.\")\n    71\t\n    72\t    def create(self, title: str, slug: str, body: str, author_id: int, *,\n    73\t               also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> int:\n    74\t        \"\"\"Create a draft.\"\"\"\n    75\t        title, slug, body = validate(title, slug, body)\n    76\t        try:\n    77\t            with db.connect() as conn:\n    78\t                item_id = conn.execute(\n    79\t                    f\"INSERT INTO {self.table} (title, slug, body, author_id)\"\n    80\t                    \" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n    81\t                    (title, slug, body, author_id),\n    82\t                ).lastrowid\n    83\t                if also:\n    84\t                    also(conn, item_id)\n    85\t        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n    86\t            raise self._duplicate_slug_error(exc, slug) from None\n    87\t        return item_id\n    88\t\n    89\t    def update(self, item_id: int, title: str, slug: str, body: str, *,\n    90\t               drafts_only: bool = False, also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> bool:\n    91\t        \"\"\"Edit title, slug, and body. The author, created_at, and status are\n    92\t        kept. With drafts_only, a published item is left alone. False if\n    93\t        nothing was changed.\"\"\"\n    94\t        title, slug, body = validate(title, slug, body)\n    95\t        try:\n    96\t            with db.connect() as conn:\n    97\t                changed = conn.execute(\n    98\t                    f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET title = ?, slug = ?, body = ?,\"\n    99\t                    \" updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n   100\t                    \" WHERE id = ? AND (status = 'draft' OR NOT ?)\",\n   101\t                    (title, slug, body, item_id, drafts_only),\n   102\t                ).rowcount == 1\n   103\t                if changed and also:\n   104\t                    also(conn, item_id)\n   105\t                return changed\n   106\t        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n   107\t            raise self._duplicate_slug_error(exc, slug) from None\n   108\t\n   109\t    def get(self, item_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n   110\t        rows = self._select(\"c.id = ?\", \"c.id\", (item_id,))\n   111\t        return rows[0] if rows else None\n   112\t\n   113\t    def list_all(self, status: str | None = None) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n   114\t        \"\"\"Every item, or only those in `status`; most recently updated first.\"\"\"\n   115\t        where, params = (\"1\", ()) if status is None else (\"c.status = ?\", (status,))\n   116\t        return self._select(where, \"c.updated_at DESC, c.id DESC\", params)\n   117\t\n   118\t    def count_by_status(self) -> dict[str, int]:\n   119\t        \"\"\"How many items are in each status, zero included, e.g.\n   120\t        {\"draft\": 2, \"published\": 0}.\"\"\"\n   121\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n   122\t            rows = conn.execute(\n   123\t                f\"SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM {self.table} GROUP BY status\").fetchall()\n   124\t        return {**dict.fromkeys(STATUS_LABELS, 0), **dict(rows)}\n   125\t\n   126\t    def list_published(self, order: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n   127\t        return self._select(\"c.status = 'published'\", order)\n   128\t\n   129\t    def get_published(self, slug: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n   130\t        \"\"\"The published item with this slug; None for a draft or no such item.\"\"\"\n   131\t        rows = self._select(\"c.status = 'published' AND c.slug = ?\", \"c.id\", (slug,))\n   132\t        return rows[0] if rows else None\n   133\t\n   134\t    def set_status(self, item_id: int, status: str) -> bool:\n   135\t        \"\"\"Publish or unpublish. False if there is no such item.\"\"\"\n   136\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n   137\t            return conn.execute(\n   138\t                f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET status = ?, updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n   139\t                \" WHERE id = ?\",\n   140\t                (status, item_id),\n   141\t            ).rowcount == 1\n   142\t\n   143\t    def delete(self, item_id: int) -> bool:\n   144\t        \"\"\"False if there is no such item.\"\"\"\n   145\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n   146\t            return conn.execute(\n   147\t                f\"DELETE FROM {self.table} WHERE id = ?\", (item_id,)).rowcount == 1\n=== app/data_bites.py\n     1\t\"\"\"Data Bites: short, dated Markdown items.\n     2\t\n     3\tAny Analyst or Director may create, edit, publish, and unpublish any Data Bite\n     4\t(shift continuity, ADR-003); only a Director may delete one, which the routes\n     5\tenforce. Editing never changes the author or created_at.\n     6\t\n     7\tPublic-facing code reads Data Bites only through `list_published` and\n     8\t`get_published`, so a draft cannot leak through it.\n     9\t\"\"\"\n    10\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n    11\t\n    12\timport sqlite3\n    13\t\n    14\tfrom app.content import ContentTable\n    15\t\n    16\t_TABLE = ContentTable(\"data_bites\", \"Data Bite\")\n    17\t\n    18\tcreate = _TABLE.create\n    19\tget = _TABLE.get\n    20\tlist_all = _TABLE.list_all\n    21\tcount_by_status = _TABLE.count_by_status\n    22\tset_status = _TABLE.set_status\n    23\tdelete = _TABLE.delete\n    24\tget_published = _TABLE.get_published\n    25\t\n    26\t\n    27\tdef update(bite_id: int, title: str, slug: str, body: str) -> bool:\n    28\t    \"\"\"Edit title, slug, and body. False if there is no such Data Bite.\"\"\"\n    29\t    return _TABLE.update(bite_id, title, slug, body)\n    30\t\n    31\t\n    32\tdef list_published() -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    33\t    \"\"\"The public-facing query: published Data Bites only, newest first.\"\"\"\n    34\t    return _TABLE.list_published(\"c.created_at DESC, c.id DESC\")\n=== app/reports.py\n     1\t\"\"\"Reports: durable, cite-able Markdown documents (the Factbook, the CDS).\n     2\t\n     3\tAny Analyst or Director may create a Report (always as a draft) and edit a\n     4\tdraft one, whoever started it (shift continuity, ADR-003). Once a Report is\n     5\tpublished only a Director may change it: `update` enforces that in the same\n     6\tstatement that writes, and the routes make publish, unpublish, and delete\n     7\tDirector only. Editing never changes the author or created_at.\n     8\t\n     9\tA Report may carry one attached PDF (checked by app.uploads). Attaching,\n    10\treplacing, or removing it follows the same lockdown as the body. The file is\n    11\tstored under settings.UPLOADS, outside site/, named by the Report's id; the\n    12\t`file_name` column says whether there is one.\n    13\t\n    14\tPublic-facing code reads Reports only through `list_published` and\n    15\t`get_published`, so a draft cannot leak through it.\n    16\t\"\"\"\n    17\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n    18\t\n    19\timport os\n    20\timport sqlite3\n    21\timport tempfile\n    22\tfrom pathlib import Path\n    23\t\n    24\tfrom app import db, settings\n    25\tfrom app.content import AlsoWrite, ContentError, ContentTable\n    26\tfrom app.uploads import Pdf\n    27\tfrom app.users import is_director\n    28\t\n    29\t_TABLE = ContentTable(\"reports\", \"Report\")\n    30\t\n    31\tget = _TABLE.get\n    32\tlist_all = _TABLE.list_all\n    33\tcount_by_status = _TABLE.count_by_status\n    34\tset_status = _TABLE.set_status\n    35\tget_published = _TABLE.get_published\n    36\t\n    37\t\n    38\tclass ReportLocked(ContentError):\n    39\t    \"\"\"A published Report, and the user is not a Director.\"\"\"\n    40\t\n    41\t\n    42\tdef can_edit(report: sqlite3.Row, user: sqlite3.Row) -> bool:\n    43\t    \"\"\"The lockdown rule. `update` and `remove_file` apply the same rule in\n    44\t    their UPDATEs.\"\"\"\n    45\t    return report[\"status\"] == \"draft\" or is_director(user)\n    46\t\n    47\t\n    48\tdef file_path(report_id: int) -> Path:\n    49\t    \"\"\"Where a Report's attached file is stored. Built from the id alone.\"\"\"\n    50\t    return settings.UPLOADS / \"reports\" / f\"{int(report_id)}.pdf\"\n    51\t\n    52\t\n    53\tdef _write_atomically(path: Path, data: bytes) -> None:\n    54\t    \"\"\"Replace `path` in one step, so a failed write never leaves half a file.\"\"\"\n    55\t    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    56\t    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, suffix=\".part\")\n    57\t    try:\n    58\t        with os.fdopen(fd, \"wb\") as f:\n    59\t            f.write(data)\n    60\t        os.replace(tmp, path)\n    61\t    except BaseException:\n    62\t        Path(tmp).unlink(missing_ok=True)\n    63\t        raise\n    64\t\n    65\t\n    66\tdef _attaching(pdf: Pdf | None) -> AlsoWrite | None:\n    67\t    \"\"\"Attach `pdf` in the same transaction as the Report's row, so the body\n    68\t    and the file are saved together or not at all.\"\"\"\n    69\t    if pdf is None:\n    70\t        return None\n    71\t\n    72\t    def attach(conn: sqlite3.Connection, report_id: int) -> None:\n    73\t        conn.execute(\"UPDATE reports SET file_name = ? WHERE id = ?\", (pdf.name, report_id))\n    74\t        _write_atomically(file_path(report_id), pdf.data)\n    75\t\n    76\t    return attach\n    77\t\n    78\t\n    79\tdef _missing_or_locked(report_id: int) -> bool:\n    80\t    \"\"\"After a guarded write changed nothing: False if there is no such\n    81\t    Report, otherwise it was published and locked.\"\"\"\n    82\t    if get(report_id) is None:\n    83\t        return False\n    84\t    raise ReportLocked(\"Only the Director can change a published Report.\")\n    85\t\n    86\t\n    87\tdef create(title: str, slug: str, body: str, author_id: int, *,\n    88\t           pdf: Pdf | None = None) -> int:\n    89\t    \"\"\"Create a draft Report, with its file if one is given.\"\"\"\n    90\t    return _TABLE.create(title, slug, body, author_id, also=_attaching(pdf))\n    91\t\n    92\t\n    93\tdef update(report_id: int, title: str, slug: str, body: str, *,\n    94\t           user: sqlite3.Row, pdf: Pdf | None = None) -> bool:\n    95\t    \"\"\"Edit title, slug, and body on behalf of `user`, and attach or replace\n    96\t    the file if one is given. False if there is no such Report; ReportLocked if\n    97\t    it is published and `user` is not a Director.\"\"\"\n    98\t    if _TABLE.update(report_id, title, slug, body, drafts_only=not is_director(user),\n    99\t                     also=_attaching(pdf)):\n   100\t        return True\n   101\t    return _missing_or_locked(report_id)\n   102\t\n   103\t\n   104\tdef remove_file(report_id: int, *, user: sqlite3.Row) -> bool:\n   105\t    \"\"\"Remove the Report's file on behalf of `user`, as `update`.\"\"\"\n   106\t    with db.connect() as conn:\n   107\t        removed = conn.execute(\n   108\t            \"UPDATE reports SET file_name = NULL, updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n   109\t            \" WHERE id = ? AND (status = 'draft' OR ?)\",\n   110\t            (report_id, is_director(user)),\n   111\t        ).rowcount == 1\n   112\t    if not removed:\n   113\t        return _missing_or_locked(report_id)\n   114\t    # Only once the row no longer names it, so a failed commit keeps the file.\n   115\t    file_path(report_id).unlink(missing_ok=True)\n   116\t    return True\n   117\t\n   118\t\n   119\tdef delete(report_id: int) -> bool:\n   120\t    \"\"\"Delete the Report and its file. False if there is no such Report.\"\"\"\n   121\t    if not _TABLE.delete(report_id):\n   122\t        return False\n   123\t    file_path(report_id).unlink(missing_ok=True)\n   124\t    return True\n   125\t\n   126\t\n   127\tdef list_published() -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n   128\t    \"\"\"The public-facing query: published Reports only, by title.\"\"\"\n   129\t    return _TABLE.list_published(\"c.title, c.id\")\n=== app/settings.py\n     1\t\"\"\"Configuration, read from the environment (never hard-code secrets).\"\"\"\n     2\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n     3\t\n     4\timport os\n     5\tfrom pathlib import Path\n     6\t\n     7\tROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n     8\t\n     9\t\n    10\tdef _load_dotenv(path: Path) -> None:\n    11\t    \"\"\"Read KEY=VALUE lines from .env into os.environ. Variables already set in\n    12\t    the real environment win.\"\"\"\n    13\t    if not path.is_file():\n    14\t        return\n    15\t    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():\n    16\t        key, sep, value = line.partition(\"=\")\n    17\t        key = key.strip()\n    18\t        if not sep or not key or key.startswith(\"#\"):\n    19\t            continue\n    20\t        os.environ.setdefault(key, value.strip().strip(\"'\\\"\"))\n    21\t\n    22\t\n    23\t_load_dotenv(ROOT / \".env\")\n    24\t\n    25\tTEMPLATES = ROOT / \"templates\"\n    26\tSITE = ROOT / \"site\"\n    27\t\n    28\tSECRET_KEY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY\", \"dev-only-not-for-production\")\n    29\tSECRET_KEY_IS_PLACEHOLDER = SECRET_KEY in (\n    30\t    \"dev-only-not-for-production\", \"[REDACTED]\")\n    31\t# A relative CMS_DATABASE is relative to the repo, not the current directory.\n    32\tDATABASE_PATH = ROOT / os.environ.get(\"CMS_DATABASE\", \"cms.db\")\n    33\t# Uploaded Report files. Outside site/, and gitignored like the database.\n    34\tUPLOADS = ROOT / os.environ.get(\"CMS_UPLOADS\", \"uploads\")\n    35\tSITE_TITLE = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SITE_TITLE\", \"My CMS\")\n    36\t# Set this to your Pages URL once you deploy, e.g.\n    37\t# https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n    38\tBASE_PATH = os.environ.get(\"CMS_BASE_PATH\", \"\")\n=== app/main.py\n     1\t\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n     2\t\n     3\tThe admin console lives under /admin (login required) and the public site\n     4\tat /. Routes live in their own modules under app/routes/ and are included\n     5\there. Keep this file small.\n     6\t\"\"\"\n     7\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n     8\t\n     9\timport sys\n    10\tfrom contextlib import asynccontextmanager\n    11\t\n    12\tfrom fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request\n    13\tfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n    14\tfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n    15\t\n    16\tfrom app import db, settings\n    17\tfrom app.auth import LoginRequired, current_user\n    18\tfrom app.routes import admin, auth, data_bites, public, reports, users\n    19\t\n    20\tSESSION_MAX_AGE = 8 * 60 * 60  # one working day\n    21\tALL_METHODS = [\"GET\", \"HEAD\", \"POST\", \"PUT\", \"PATCH\", \"DELETE\", \"OPTIONS\"]\n    22\t\n    23\t\n    24\t@asynccontextmanager\n    25\tasync def lifespan(app: FastAPI):\n    26\t    # At server start, not import, so importing app.main never touches a database.\n    27\t    db.init_db()\n    28\t    if settings.SECRET_KEY_IS_PLACEHOLDER:\n    29\t        print(\"WARNING: CMS_SECRET_KEY is unset or the .env.example placeholder; \"\n    30\t              \"session cookies can be forged. Set a long random value in .env.\",\n    31\t              file=sys.stderr)\n    32\t    yield\n    33\t\n    34\t\n    35\tdef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    36\t    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\", lifespan=lifespan)\n    37\t    app.add_middleware(\n    38\t        SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n    39\t        session_cookie=\"cms_session\", max_age=SESSION_MAX_AGE, same_site=\"lax\",\n    40\t    )\n    41\t\n    42\t    @app.exception_handler(LoginRequired)\n    43\t    def redirect_to_login(request: Request, exc: LoginRequired):\n    44\t        return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\n    45\t\n    46\t    app.include_router(public.router)\n    47\t    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    48\t    app.include_router(admin.router)\n    49\t    app.include_router(users.router)\n    50\t    app.include_router(data_bites.router)\n    51\t    app.include_router(reports.router)\n    52\t\n    53\t    # Must stay last: any /admin request no router above claimed, by path or by\n    54\t    # method. It holds only the user's id and a CSRF token. The user is\n     5\tre-loaded from the database on every protected request, so deactivating an\n     6\taccount ends its sessions at once.\n     7\t\"\"\"\n     8\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n     9\t\n    10\timport secrets\n    11\timport sqlite3\n    12\t\n    13\tfrom fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, Request\n    14\t\n    15\tfrom app import users\n    16\t\n    17\t\n    18\tclass LoginRequired(Exception):\n    19\t    \"\"\"Raised by current_user; main.py turns it into a redirect to /login.\"\"\"\n    20\t\n    21\t\n    22\tdef current_user(request: Request) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    23\t    \"\"\"Dependency: the logged-in, still-active user, or LoginRequired.\"\"\"\n    24\t    user_id = request.session.get(\"user_id\")\n    25\t    user = users.get_active_user(user_id) if user_id is not None else None\n    26\t    if user is None:\n    27\t        request.session.clear()\n    28\t        raise LoginRequired\n    29\t    return user\n    30\t\n    31\t\n    32\tdef require_director(user: sqlite3.Row = Depends(current_user)) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    33\t    \"\"\"Dependency: current_user, but 403 unless they are a Director.\"\"\"\n    34\t    if not users.is_director(user):\n    35\t        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Directors only.\")\n    36\t    return user\n    37\t\n    38\t\n    39\tdef log_in(request: Request, user: sqlite3.Row) -> None:\n    40\t    # A fresh session (and CSRF token) on login, so a pre-login cookie planted\n    41\t    # by someone else never becomes an authenticated one.\n    42\t    request.session.clear()\n    43\t    request.session[\"user_id\"] = user[\"id\"]\n    44\t    csrf_token(request)\n    45\t\n    46\t\n    47\tdef log_out(request: Request) -> None:\n    48\t    request.session.clear()\n    49\t\n    50\t\n    51\tdef csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:\n    52\t    \"\"\"The session's CSRF token, created on first use. Templates call this.\"\"\"\n    53\t    token = request.session.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    54\t    if token is None:\n    55\t        token = request.session[\"csrf_token\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    56\t    return token\n    57\t\n    58\t\n    59\tasync def require_csrf(request: Request) -> None:\n    60\t    \"\"\"Dependency for every state-changing POST: the form's csrf_token must\n    61\t    match the session's.\"\"\"\n    62\t    form = await request.form()\n    63\t    submitted = form.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    64\t    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    65\t    if not (isinstance(submitted, str) and expected\n    66\t            and secrets.compare_digest(submitted, expected)):\n    67\t        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Invalid or missing CSRF token.\")\n\"\"\"T07: Public site pages (issue #8).\n\nThe live public pages sit at the same paths `cms publish` will export them to,\nso every link between them is relative and works in both places.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom posixpath import dirname, join, normpath\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom tests.conftest import backdate, post_form\nfrom tests.test_t03_data_bites import BITE, create_bite\nfrom tests.test_t04_reports import REPORT, create_report\nfrom tests.test_t05_report_files import PDF, pdf, post_with_file, reports_file\n\n\ndef published_bite(c: TestClient, **override) -> str:\n    bite = create_bite(c, **override)\n    assert post_form(c, f\"/admin/data-bites/{bite}/publish\", {}).status_code == 303\n    return bite\n\n\ndef test_visitor_reads_a_published_data_bite(client_as, client):\n Markdown body is rendered, not shown raw.\n    assert \"<strong>1,745</strong>\" in response.text\n\n\ndef test_a_draft_data_bite_has_no_public_page(client_as, client):\n    analyst = client_as(\"editor\")\n    bite = published_bite(analyst)\n    create_bite(analyst, slug=\"unreleased\", title=\"Unreleased count\")\n\n    assert client.get(\"/data-bites/unreleased.html\").status_code == 404\n    assert client.get(\"/data-bites/no-such-bite.html\").status_code == 404\n    # Unpublishing takes the page down again.\n    post_form(analyst, f\"/admin/data-bites/{bite}/unpublish\", {})\n    assert client.get(\"/data-bites/fall-enrollment.html\").status_code == 404\n\n\ndef test_visitor_lists_published_data_bites_newest_first(client_as, client):\n    analyst = client_as(\"editor\")\n    older = published_bite(analyst)\n    backdate(\"data_bites\", older)\n    published_bite(analyst, slug=\"spring-survey\", title=\"Spring survey results\")\n    create_bite(analyst, slug=\"unreleased\", title=\"Unreleased count\")\n\n    page = client.get(\"/data-bites/index.html\")\n    assert page.status_code == 200\n    assert page.text.index(\"Spring survey results\") < page.text.index(BITE[\"title\"])\n    # Each links to its page, page.text\n    assert client.get(\"/data-bites/\").text == page.text\n\n\ndef published_report(director: TestClient, **override) -> str:\n    rid = create_report(director, **override)\n    assert post_form(director, f\"/admin/reports/{rid}/publish\", {}).status_code == 303\n    return rid\n\n\ndef test_visitor_reads_a_published_report_and_downloads_its_file(client_as, client):\n    director = 'href=\"../reports/files/factbook.pdf\"' in page.text\n\n\"\"\"T03: Data Bites (issue #4).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom tests.conftest import backdate, post_form, second_analyst\n\nBITE = {\"title\": \"Fall enrollment snapshot\", \"slug\": \"fall-enrollment\",\n        \"body\": \"Enrollment is **1,745** this fall.\"}\n\n\ndef bite_row(c: TestClient, slug: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"This Data Bite's row of the admin list, as HTML.\"\"\"\n    for row in c.get(\"/admin/data-bites\").text.split(\"<tr\")[1:]:\n        if f\"<code>{slug}</code>\" in row:\n            return row\n    raise AssertionError(f\"{slug} is not listed\")\n\n\ndef bite_id(c:  assert response.headers[\"location\"] == \"/admin/data-bites\"\n\n    row = bite_row(analyst, BITE[\"slug\"])\n    assert BITE[\"title\"] in row and \"Draft\" in row\n\n\ndef bytes:\n    return struct.pack(\">I\", len(data)) + kind + data + struct.pack(\">I\", zlib.crc32(kind + data))\n\n\n# A real 1x1 PNG, and minimal JPEG and WebP files with the right signatures.\nPNG = 5) + b\"\\x2f\\x00\\x00\\x00\\x00\" + b\"\\x00\"\nWEBP = b\"RIFF\" + struct.pack(\"<I\", 4 + len(_VP8L)) + b\"WEBP\" + _VP8L\n\n\ndef png(name: str = \"fall-by-class.png\", content: bytes = PNG, declared: str = \"image/png\"):\n    return (name, content, declared)\n\n\ndef upload(c: TestClient, bid: str, file, *, with_csrf=True):\n    data = {\"csrf_token\": csrf_from(c.get(\"/admin\").text)}    folder = settings.UPLOADS / \"images\" / \"data-bites\" / bid\n    return sorted(p.name for p in folder.iterdir()) if folder.exists() else []\n\n\ndef edit_bite(c: TestClient, bid: str, test_any_analyst_or_the_director_uploads_to_any_data_bite_draft_or_published(client_as):\n    director = client_as(\"admin\")\n    riley = second_analyst(director)\n    draft = {"parentUuid":"ac73c7e4-9d2f-483e-b2ec-5dc5b9410c9e","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfY8T4bKmiZcBBEKotiPq","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01QbMYTmoeF8FfTKyTQDqZD5","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/chart_images.py","content":"\"\"\"Chart images: the PNG, JPEG, or WebP pictures a Data Bite or Report shows in\nits Markdown body as `image:<name>` (ADR-004).\n\nAn image belongs to one item, named here by its kind (\"data-bites\" or\n\"reports\") and id, and is stored at settings.UPLOADS/images/<kind>/<id>/<name>,\noutside site/. The files there are the record; there is no table. An image's\nname is its upload's filename, sanitized and lowercased, so it is safe in a\npath and in a URL, and uploading a name the item already has replaces that\nimage.\n\nAn upload is checked the way app.uploads checks a Report's PDF: the extension\nand the browser's declared type must agree, and then the bytes must carry that\nformat's signature. There is no image library (pyproject.toml is fixed), so\nthe check is by signature, not by decoding. SVG is refused: it is a document\nthat can carry script.\n\nWho may add or remove an item's images is decided by that item's module, not\nhere.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport shutil\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom fastapi import UploadFile\n\nfrom app import settings, uploads\nfrom app.content import ContentError\n\nMIB = uploads.MIB\nMAX_BYTES = 5 * MIB\nMAX_PER_ITEM = 10\nKINDS = {\"data-bites\": \"Data Bite\", \"reports\": \"Report\"}  # kind: noun, for messages\n# How near the end a format's end marker must be, allowing for trailing bytes.\n_TAIL = 1024\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass _Format:\n    label: str\n    media_type: str\n    looks_valid: Callable[[bytes], bool]\n\n\ndef _png(data: bytes) -> bool:\n    # The 8-byte signature, and the IEND chunk (with its fixed CRC) at the end.\n    return data.startswith(b\"\\x89PNG\\r\\n\\x1a\\n\") and b\"IEND\\xaeB`\\x82\" in data[-_TAIL:]\n\n\ndef _jpeg(data: bytes) -> bool:\n    # Start-of-image, then end-of-image at the end.\n    return data.startswith(b\"\\xff\\xd8\\xff\") and b\"\\xff\\xd9\" in data[-_TAIL:]\n\n\ndef _webp(data: bytes) -> bool:\n    # A RIFF container of type WEBP, holding at least as many bytes as it says.\n    return (data[:4] == b\"RIFF\" and data[8:12] == b\"WEBP\"\n            and int.from_bytes(data[4:8], \"little\") + 8 <= len(data))\n\n\n_PNG = _Format(\"PNG\", \"image/png\", _png)\n_JPEG = _Format(\"JPEG\", \"image/jpeg\", _jpeg)\n_FORMATS = {\"png\": _PNG, \"jpg\": _JPEG, \"jpeg\": _JPEG, \"webp\": _Format(\"WebP\", \"image/webp\", _webp)}\n# What read() can name an image. Anything else, e.g. from a URL, names none.\n_NAME = re.compile(r\"[a-z0-9_-]+\\.(?:png|jpe?g|webp)\")\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Image:\n    name: str   # sanitized: safe in a path and a URL\n    data: bytes\n\n\ndef read(upload: UploadFile | None) -> Image:\n    \"\"\"The upload as a checked image. ContentError, with a message safe to\n    show, if no file was chosen or it is not an acceptable image.\"\"\"\n    if upload is None or not upload.filename:\n        raise ContentError(\"Choose an image to upload.\")\n    stem, extension = uploads.split_filename(upload.filename)\n    image_format = _FORMATS.get(extension)\n    if image_format is None or upload.content_type != image_format.media_type:\n        raise ContentError(\"Only PNG, JPEG, or WebP images can be uploaded.\")\n    data = upload.file.read(MAX_BYTES + 1)\n    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:\n        raise ContentError(f\"That image is over the {MAX_BYTES // MIB} MB limit.\")\n    if not image_format.looks_valid(data):\n        raise ContentError(f\"That file is not a valid {image_format.label} image.\")\n    return Image(f\"{uploads.safe_stem(stem, 'chart').lower()}.{extension}\", data)\n\n\ndef media_type(name: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The type to serve a stored image's name with.\"\"\"\n    return _FORMATS[name.rpartition(\".\")[2]].media_type\n\n\ndef _folder(kind: str, item_id: int) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Where an item's images are stored. Built from fixed kinds and the id.\"\"\"\n    if kind not in KINDS:\n        raise ValueError(kind)\n    return settings.UPLOADS / \"images\" / kind / str(int(item_id))\n\n\ndef stored(kind: str, item_id: int) -> dict[str, Path]:\n    \"\"\"The item's images, {name: where it is stored}, by name.\"\"\"\n    folder = _folder(kind, item_id)\n    if not folder.is_dir():\n        return {}\n    return {path.name: path for path in sorted(folder.iterdir())\n            if _NAME.fullmatch(path.name) and path.is_file()}\n\n\ndef save(kind: str, item_id: int, image: Image) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Add the image to the item, or replace the one of the same name.\n    ContentError if that would be one more than MAX_PER_ITEM.\"\"\"\n    existing = stored(kind, item_id)\n    if image.name not in existing and len(existing) >= MAX_PER_ITEM:\n        raise ContentError(f\"This {KINDS[kind]} already has {MAX_PER_ITEM} images, the \"\n                           \"most allowed. Delete one to add another.\")\n    uploads.write_atomically(_folder(kind, item_id) / image.name, image.data)\n\n\ndef remove(kind: str, item_id: int, name: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"False if the item has no image of that name.\"\"\"\n    path = stored(kind, item_id).get(name)\n    if path is None:\n        return False\n    path.unlink(missing_ok=True)\n    return True\n\n\ndef remove_all(kind: str, item_id: int) -> None:\n    shutil.rmtree(_folder(kind, item_id), ignore_errors=True)\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1380,"cache_read_input_tokens":127738,"output_tokens":10744,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":7245},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1380,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":10744,"cache_read_input_tokens":127738,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1380,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1380},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01QbMYTmoeF8FfTKyTQDqZD5":{"file_path":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/chart_images.py","content":"\"\"\"Chart images: the PNG, JPEG, or WebP pictures a Data Bite or Report shows in\nits Markdown body as `image:<name>` (ADR-004).\n\nAn image belongs to one item, named here by its kind (\"data-bites\" or\n\"reports\") and id, and is stored at settings.UPLOADS/images/<kind>/<id>/<name>,\noutside site/. SVG is refused: it is a document\nthat can carry script.\n\nWho may add or remove an item's images is decided by that item's module, not\nhere.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport shutil\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom fastapi import UploadFile\n\nfrom app import settings, uploads\nfrom app.content import ContentError\n\nMIB = uploads.MIB\nMAX_BYTES = 5 * MIB\nMAX_PER_ITEM = 10\nKINDS = {\"data-bites\": \"Data Bite\", \"reports\": \"Report\"}  # kind: noun, for messages\n# How near the end a format's end marker must be, allowing for trailing bytes.\n_TAIL = 1024\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass _Format:\n    label: str\n    media_type: str\n    looks_valid: Callable[[bytes], bool]\n\n\ndef _png(data: bytes) -> bool:\n    # The 8-byte signature, and the IEND chunk (with its fixed CRC) at the end.\n    return data.startswith(b\"\\x89PNG\\r\\n\\x1a\\n\") and b\"IEND\\xaeB`\\x82\" in data[-_TAIL:]\n\n\ndef _jpeg(data: bytes) -> bool:\n    # Start-of-image, then end-of-image at the end.\n    return data.startswith(b\"\\xff\\xd8\\xff\") and b\"\\xff\\xd9\" in data[-_TAIL:]\n\n\ndef _webp(data: bytes) -> bool:\n    # A RIFF container of type WEBP, holding at least as many bytes as it says.\n    return (data[:4] == b\"RIFF\" and data[8:12] == b\"WEBP\"\n            and int.from_bytes(data[4:8], \"little\") + 8 <= len(data))\n\n\n_PNG = _Format(\"PNG\", \"image/png\", _png)\n_JPEG = _Format(\"JPEG\", \"image/jpeg\", _jpeg)\n_FORMATS = {\"png\": _PNG, \"jpg\": _JPEG, \"jpeg\": _JPEG, \"webp\": _Format(\"WebP\", \"image/webp\", _webp)}\n# What read() can name an image. Anything else, e.g. from a URL, names none.\n_NAME = re.compile(r\"[a-z0-9_-]+\\.(?:png|jpe?g|webp)\")\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Image:\n    name: str   # sanitized: safe in a path and a URL\n    data: bytes\n\n\ndef read(upload: UploadFile | None) -> Image:\n    \"\"\"The upload as a checked image. ContentError, with a message safe to\n    show, if no file was chosen or it is not an acceptable image.\"\"\"\n    if upload is None or not upload.filename:\n        raise ContentError(\"Choose an image to upload.\")\n    stem, extension = uploads.split_filename(upload.filename)\n    image_format = _FORMATS.get(extension)\n    if image_format is None or upload.content_type != image_format.media_type:\n        raise ContentError(\"Only PNG, JPEG, or WebP images can be uploaded.\")\n    data = upload.file.read(MAX_BYTES + 1)\n    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:\n        raise ContentError(f\"That image is over the {MAX_BYTES // MIB} MB limit.\")\n    if not image_format.looks_valid(data):\n        raise ContentError(f\"That file is not a valid {image_format.label} image.\")\n    return Image(f\"{uploads.safe_stem(stem, 'chart').lower()}.{extension}\", data)\n\n\ndef media_type(name: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The type to serve a stored image's name with.\"\"\"\n    return _FORMATS[name.rpartition(\".\")[2]].media_type\n\n\ndef _folder(kind: str, item_id: int) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Where an item's images are stored. Built from fixed kinds and the id.\"\"\"\n    if kind not in KINDS:\n        raise ValueError(kind)\n    return settings.UPLOADS / \"images\" / kind / str(int(item_id))\n\n\ndef stored(kind: str, item_id: int) -> dict[str, Path]:\n    \"\"\"The item's images, {name: where it is stored}, by name.\"\"\"\n    folder = _folder(kind, item_id)\n    if not folder.is_dir():\n        return {}\n    return {path.name: path for path in sorted(folder.iterdir())\n            if _NAME.fullmatch(path.name) and path.is_file()}\n\n\ndef save(kind: str, item_id: int, image: Image) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Add the image to the item, or replace the one of the same name.\n    ContentError if that would be one more than MAX_PER_ITEM.\"\"\"\n    existing = stored(kind, item_id)\n    if image.name not in existing and len(existing) >= MAX_PER_ITEM:\n        raise ContentError(f\"This {KINDS[kind]} already has {MAX_PER_ITEM} images, the \"\n                           \"most allowed. Delete one to add another.\")\n    uploads.write_atomically(_folder(kind, item_id) / image.name, image.data)\n\n\ndef remove(kind: str, item_id: int, name: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"False if the item has no image of that name.\"\"\"\n    path = stored(kind, item_id).get(name)\n    if path is None:\n        return False\n    path.unlink(missing_ok=True)\n    return True\n\n\ndef remove_all(kind: str, item_id: int) -> None:\n    shutil.rmtree(_folder(kind, item_id), ignore_errors=True)\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"b6cfe05c-e043-4a4c-b81c-3de675b7e357","session_id":"fc138a42-1eee-4017-bff2-c6a77302f820","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"1994cc11-b04f-4e5a-9581-ac76c08df346","version":"2.1.284","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"c57b7f4c-3568-48b2-bc48-7096c395c808","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"0fc927ce-631b-435e-a5e8-f12b4414d456","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/davelleat/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Review uncommitted changes since HEAD (9577cac) for ticket T10, issue #12 (spec #11)."}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"1f36f005-e2c0-4e8d-88b1-42a7234636db","timestamp":"2026-09-29T17:37:01.370Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_014vTkh6t8HB71qzZ94uAJMS","session_id":"fc138a42-1eee-4017-bff2-c6a77302f820","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"1994cc11-b04f-4e5a-9581-ac76c08df346","version":"2.1.284","gitBranch":"main"}

The diff meets every documented standard I checked it against. Everything below is a judgement call.\n\n**Documented standards that pass**\n- **Relative paths (CLAUDE.md):** `Page.render` builds `image_src` from `root`, so the public page gets `../images/...`. The absolute `/admin/...` URLs appear only in the admin console.\n- **CSRF (CLAUDE.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST #3):** all three new POSTs (`preview`, `images`, `images/{name}/delete`) use `require_csrf`, and both new forms carry the token.\n- **Sanitize Markdown (#7):** the `image:` rewrite runs before `nh3.clean`, and other image URLs still go to the sanitizer.\n- **Drafts stay out of `site/` (#8):** `files()` iterates `list_published()`, and `data_bite_image` goes through `get_published`.\n- **Dependencies:** none added. The signature check follows ADR-004.\n- **CSS prefix (user rule):** `.content-body img`, `.content-images`, `.content-images-list` and `.content-image-warning` are all scoped.\n\n**Minor standards points (soft)**\n- **CONTEXT.md vocabulary:** the glossary term is \"Chart image\", but the code uses bare \"image\" throughout (`images()`, `add_image`, `remove_image`, `IMAGE_REFERENCE`, route `image`). \"Image\" isn't on the Avoid list, so this is only drift. Separately, the `app/uploads.py` docstring hunk keeps \"a Report's attachment\". The glossary word for that is \"attached file\", and \"attachment\" is on the Avoid list. The phrase predates this diff, but the diff edits that sentence.\n- **Idiom drift in `app/routes/data_bites.py`:** it computes `chart_images.MAX_BYTES // chart_images.MIB` inline. `routes/reports.py` uses a module constant, `_MAX_FILE_MB`.\n- **Import order in the test file:** `from html.parser import HTMLParser` comes before `import zlib`. There is no linter configured to catch this.\n\n**Possible smells (baseline)**\n- **Duplicated Code:** `FileResponse(path, media_type=chart_images.media_type(name), headers={\"X-Content-Type-Options\": \"nosniff\"})` appears in both `routes/data_bites.py:image` and `routes/public.py:data_bite_image`. With the two existing PDF routes, that makes four copies of the nosniff response. Separately, `{data_bite_image_path(bite[\"slug\"], name) ... data_bites.images(bite[\"id\"])}` is built twice in `public_site.py` (`_data_bite_page` and `files()`).\n- **Duplicated Code / Speculative Generality:** `rendering.render_markdown` has `image_src or None  # a template may pass Undefined`, and `_content_fields.html` also has `image_src | default(none)`. Both guard against the same thing.\n- **Primitive Obsession / Shotgun Surgery:** the kind string `\"data-bites\"` appears in `data_bites._IMAGES`, `chart_images.KINDS`, the `images/data-bites/` path and the route. `KINDS` also repeats the nouns `ContentTable(\"data_bites\", \"Data Bite\")` already holds.\n- **Speculative Generality:** `KINDS` includes `\"reports\": \"Report\"`, but T10 wires up only Data Bites. ADR-004 covers Reports, so this can be defended.\n- **Inconsistent use of `touch(also=...)`:** `add_image` writes the file inside the transaction, as `touch`'s docstring describes. `remove_image` calls `_TABLE.touch(bite_id)` first and then `chart_images.remove(...)` outside it, so a failed unlink still bumps `updated_at`. Passing `also=` there would match the pattern.\n- **Mysterious Name:** the admin route handler is just `image`. Neighbouring handlers are named by action (`upload_image`, `delete_image`, and `download_file` in reports), so `serve_image` would fit better.\n- **Middle Man:** `chart_images.MIB = uploads.MIB` only re-exports the constant so the routes can reach it.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>69270</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>3</tool_uses><duration_ms>40765</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>I found no missing requirements and nothing that looks wrong enough to block T10. The app tests all pass. The 14 failing tests are in `tests/test_ctx_guard.py` and `tests/test_usage_report.py`, which are session tooling and not touched by this diff. There are two things worth fixing or writing down, both under (c).\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n\nNone. Every acceptance criterion has matching code and a test: upload by any role on a draft or published bite, the snippet, content checks, the 5 MB and 10-image limits, replace and delete, rendering in all three places, the empty-description warning, the draft gate, cleanup on delete, and login and CSRF.\n\n**(b) Scope creep, all small**\n\n- `ContentTable.touch` changes a Data Bite's `updated_at` whenever an image is added or removed. No criterion asks for this. It is harmless, but \"Last updated\" will now move on image changes.\n- `write_atomically` and `split_filename` moved from the Report code into `app/uploads.py`. This is reuse for the new image code, not new behaviour.\n- Also added: a new route, `POST /admin/data-bites/{id}/preview`, so the live preview can show images; a `.content-body img { max-width: 100% }` style; and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on image responses. Each supports a stated requirement.\n\n**(c) Implemented, but check these**\n\n1. **Export test relaxed.** The spec says: \"the export stays byte-identical to the live site (T08's crawl test), now including images.\" The T08 test checks that the export and the crawled site have exactly the same files. The T10 test instead allows one extra file: an uploaded image the body doesn't use. That image is exported, and served at its URL, but no page links to it, so the crawl can't find it. It's a reasonable reading of \"published with it\", but it is a change from what the spec says. Either record it in ADR-004 or only export images the body references.\n2. **\"Deleting a Data Bite deletes its images.\"** `data_bites.delete` deletes the database row first, then the image folder with `shutil.rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True)`. The ids are `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` without `AUTOINCREMENT` (`app/db.py`), so SQLite can reuse the id of the newest deleted bite. If that folder delete fails silently, the next Data Bite with that id takes over the old images, and they go public when it is published.\n\n**T11 reuse**\n\nThe ticket promises: \"This ticket builds the shared image code (validation, storage, the `image:` rewrite …, the public and export paths) that T11 reuses for Reports.\"\n\n- **Reusable as is:** `app/chart_images.py` (it already knows about `\"reports\"`), `render_markdown(image_src)` and `images_without_description`, `Page.images`, and `templates/admin/_chart_images.html`.\n- **T11 will have to copy, not reuse:**\n  - The empty-description warning markup is written into `data_bite_edit.html` rather than a shared partial.\n  - `_image_src`, the preview route and the upload, serve and delete routes live in `app/routes/data_bites.py`.\n  - `public_site.files()` and the public image route only handle Data Bites. That's expected, since the ticket leaves Report paths to T11.\n\nNone of this breaks the promise. Moving the warning into a partial now would save T11 the duplication.\n\nThe diff under review is `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/1994cc11-b04f-4e5a-9581-ac76c08df346/scratchpad/t10.diff`.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>66830</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>6</tool_uses><duration_ms>121668</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

Nothing is missing.\n\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| **(c) Id reuse:** `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` ids can be reused. If a deleted Data Bite's image folder survived (`rmtree(ignore_errors=True)`), a new Data Bite would inherit, and later publish, its images. | **Fixed:** `data_bites.create` clears any leftover folder for its id in the same transaction, and `remove_all` no longer swallows errors. New test: `test_a_new_data_bite_never_inherits_images_left_under_its_id`. |\n| **(c) Export vs crawl:** an uploaded image the body doesn't place is exported, but no crawl reaches it, so T10's parity test allows that one extra file | **Kept, and recorded in ADR-004.** The spec gates per item (\"an image is public only while its item is published\"), so every image on a published item is public, placed or not. The extra file is still byte-identical to what the app serves at that path, and the test checks this. |\n| **T11 reuse:** the empty-description warning was inline in `data_bite_edit.html` | **Fixed:** moved to `admin/_undescribed_images.html`, which sits beside `admin/_chart_images.html` for T11 |\n| (b) `ContentTable.touch`: an image change moves the item's \"Last updated\" | **Kept.** Changing a chart changes the item. T11 needs the same guarded write for the Report lockdown. |\n| (b) New `/admin/data-bites/{id}/preview` route, `.content-body img` CSS, nosniff | **Kept.** Each supports a stated requirement (the preview shows images, images fit the column, no sniffing). |\n\nTests: 46 in `tests/test_t10_chart_images.py`; 235 across the app suites (T00–T10). The 14 failures in `test_ctx_guard.py` and `test_usage_report.py` are the course exercise stubs and were already failing before this change. Also checked in the running app: upload, SVG rejected, draft image 404, publish, public page shows the chart, admin live preview shows it.\nEOF\ngh issue comment 12 --body-file $S/review-comment.md && gh issue view 12 --comments --json comments -q '.comments[-1].url'","description":"Post code-review findings on issue #12"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1089,"cache_read_input_tokens":186409,"output_tokens":1637,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1089,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1637,"cache_read_input_tokens":186409,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1089,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1089},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_015QDgtLcBmn5CGWyu3boXdZ":{"command":"cd /Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms && S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/1994cc11-b04f-4e5a-9581-ac76c08df346/scratchpad && cat > $S/review-comment.md <<'EOF'\n## /code-review: T10 (Standards and Spec reviews, working tree against 9577cac)\n\n### Standards\nThe reviewer found no hard violations. {"parentUuid":"4d06f215-ab04-4b91-9e14-1106ed63aaf0","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfY9FKdyvqMb4kGsmZMLM","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"T10 (#12, chart images on Data Bites) is done and committed as `1a5a02d` on `main`. I haven't pushed it, so #12 stays open until you push (the commit ends `Closes #12`).\n\n**What it does:** Analysts and the Director can upload PNG, JPEG or WebP charts on a Data Bite's edit page, and delete them there. The page lists each image with a `![Description](image:<name>)` line to paste into the body. That reference shows the chart in the preview, on the public page and in the `cms publish` export, at `images/data-bites/<slug>/<name>`. Images are only public while their Data Bite is published. Unpublishing takes them down, and deleting the Data Bite deletes them.\n\n**Tests:** all 46 new tests pass, and the app suites (T00–T10) pass at 235. The full suite shows 14 failures, all in `test_ctx_guard.py` and `test_usage_report.py`. Those are the course exercise stubs that raise \"implement me\", and they failed the same way before I changed anything. There's no typechecker in the fixed stack, so I only compile-checked the code.\n\n**Checked in the running app:** on a scratch database (server since stopped), an SVG upload was rejected and a draft's image returned 404. After publishing, the public page showed the chart inline, and the edit page's live preview kept showing it while I typed. The admin console has no styling, but that was already the case: its pages point at a `style.css` that doesn't exist.\n\n**Code review:** the findings and what I did about each are posted on #12 ([comment](https://github.com/DavelleAT/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/12#issuecomment-5895482140)). Neither review found anything blocking. The two that mattered:\n- **Bug, fixed:** SQLite can give a new Data Bite the id of a deleted one. If a deleted one's images had been left on disk, the new one would have picked them up and published them. A new Data Bite now clears anything left under its id, and there's a test for it.\n- **Spec decision, kept and written into ADR-004:** an image uploaded to a published Data Bite is public straight away, even before the body uses it. That follows the spec's rule that an image is public while its item is published. The practical rule for Analysts: put charts that aren't ready yet on a draft.\n\nA few smaller cleanups made T11 (Reports) easier, mainly the upload checks and the image list and warning moved into shared pieces it can reuse.\n\nI left `notes/usage-ledger.csv` and the session 11 transcript out of this commit, since those have gone in separate `docs:` commits before."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":958,"cache_read_input_tokens":189245,"output_tokens":879,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":24},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":958,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":879,"cache_read_input_tokens":189245,"cache_creation_input_tokens":958,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":958},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CfY9FKEBFF2G8qbTW47HY","type":"assistant","uuid":"6e657f99-de0b-4f9c-98ed-eb74aa761c5b","timestamp":"2026-09-29T17:42:08.420Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"fc138a42-1eee-4017-bff2-c6a77302f820","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"1994cc11-b04f-4e5a-9581-ac76c08df346","version":"2.1.284","gitBranch":"main"}

(Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)\\n- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it.
